summary: The change adds a per-extension host token that the workspace proxy injects and the SDK checks. It also adds viewer identity headers, sync access gating, a denylist for extension tool calls, and app-sharing validators. It is not ready. The workspace proxy now sets a header to `undefined` on every owner request. That makes Node's `http.request` throw, so local extension HTTP requests and WebSocket upgrades fail. None of the workspace-server or control-plane changes are covered by any test.

findings.body: `request.headers["x-halo-viewer-email"] = viewerEmail;` assigns `undefined` for every non-gateway request (line 153 yields `undefined` when `fromGateway` is false) and for any gateway request without an email header. httpxy copies `req.headers` with `outgoing.headers = { ...req.headers }` (node_modules/httpxy/dist/index.mjs:60) and passes the result to `http.request`. Node's ClientRequest calls `setHeader` for each key, and `validateHeaderValue` throws ERR_HTTP_INVALID_HEADER_VALUE when the value is `undefined`. As a result, every local Electron extension request becomes a 502, and `proxyUpgrade` WebSocket upgrades fail the same way. Lines 118 and 72-74 have the same problem when `getHostToken` returns `undefined`, for example during a restart window. Set these headers only when the value is defined, and delete them otherwise. When the host token is missing, return an error status rather than forwarding the request.

No test loads extensionProxy.ts, ExtensionHost.ts, startExtension.ts, extensionsRouter.ts, or apps/control-plane/src/workspace/proxy.ts, so 41 changed lines are uncovered. These are the security-relevant parts of the change: token injection, stripping spoofed viewer headers from non-gateway requests, and generating and rotating the host token. A test that proxies a real request through `serveExtensionRequest` to a local HTTP server would have caught F1. Add tests that check: the token header reaches the target; client-supplied `x-halo-viewer-*` and `x-halo-extension-token` headers are replaced or stripped when `fromGateway` is false; the email header is absent when no email exists; and the WebSocket upgrade path works.

The denylist is tested only as a pure function. Nothing checks that `extensionToolRouter.invoke` rejects a denied path with badRequest and never calls `toolRuntime.invokePath`, or that allowed paths still reach the runtime. Add a router-level test with a stub `toolRuntime`.

The SDK test checks only `syncAccess: "actions"` with a public viewer. It does not check that `read-only` blocks `/sync/push` but allows `/sync/pull`, that `shared` allows push, or that the owner role bypasses the gate. The `viewer` procedure is defined in the router, but the test never calls it with a valid token. Nothing checks that viewer headers are parsed into `context.viewer`, for example that an unknown role falls back to owner, that a member keeps its email, or that `/api/viewer` returns the expected viewer.

testRequests.target: packages/workspace-server/src/extensions/extensionProxy.ts:146-158 and 111-118 (serveExtensionRequest end-to-end to a stub HTTP server, fromGateway false and true)
testRequests.rationale: Would catch F1. It must check that the request succeeds, that the host token is injected, that spoofed viewer headers are replaced, and that no undefined header is sent.
The WebSocket path has the same undefined-header risk and is currently uncovered.

testRequests.target: packages/workspace-server/src/extensions/extensionsRouter.ts:39-40 (denied path returns badRequest and does not invoke the runtime)
testRequests.rationale: The policy must be enforced at the RPC boundary, not only in the helper.

testRequests.target: packages/workspace-server/src/extensions/ExtensionHost.ts:124-125,229-230,249 and startExtension.ts:49 (a host token is created, passed to the child environment, rotated on restart, and cleared on removal)
testRequests.rationale: Token lifecycle wiring is currently uncovered.

testRequests.target: apps/control-plane/src/workspace/proxy.ts:280-283 (client-supplied viewer and extension-token headers are stripped before forwarding)
testRequests.rationale: This guards an anti-spoofing invariant. A future edit to the header handling could silently let visitors claim the owner role or forge the host token.

testRequests.target: packages/extension-sdk/src/server.ts:137-151 (viewer parsing and the read-only, shared, and owner sync gate)
testRequests.rationale: Only actions mode is exercised now, and viewer parsing is never asserted.
